name: Amaziah
charge: Bringing home the gods of Seir and bowing to them
summary: Having beaten Edom with the Lord's help, Amaziah brought back the gods of the children of Seir, set them up as his gods, and burned incense to them. A prophet asked why he sought gods that could not deliver their own people; the king told him to stop before he was smitten.
offense: Amaziah did right, but not with a perfect heart. He executed the servants who had murdered his father while sparing their children, according to the law that each should die for his own sin. He also obeyed the man of God who told him to dismiss the hired Israelite troops, accepting the loss of the hundred talents he had paid. After defeating Edom, however, Amaziah brought home its gods, bowed before them, and burned incense to them. When a prophet asked why he sought gods that could not deliver their own people, the king threatened him. Lifted up by victory, he then challenged Israel and refused the warning against provoking his own hurt.
judgment: The prophet declared that God had determined to destroy Amaziah because he had done this and rejected counsel. Israel defeated Judah, captured Amaziah, broke down four hundred cubits of Jerusalem's wall, and carried away treasure and hostages. Amaziah survived the defeat, but his turning away was followed by conspiracy. He fled to Lachish, where his pursuers killed him. Earlier acts of obedience did not authorize later idolatry. The gods he had carried home could neither preserve Edom nor secure the king who adopted them.

verses.text: Now it came to pass, after that Amaziah was come from the slaughter of the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them.

Wherefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against Amaziah, and he sent unto him a prophet, which said unto him, Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?

And it came to pass, as he talked with him, that the king said unto him, Art thou made of the king’s counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten? Then the prophet forbare, and said, I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this, and hast not hearkened unto my counsel.
Then Amaziah king of Judah took advice, and sent to Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, Come, let us see one another in the face.

And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in Lebanon, and trode down the thistle.

Thou sayest, Lo, thou hast smitten the Edomites; and thine heart lifteth thee up to boast: abide now at home; why shouldest thou meddle to thine hurt, that thou shouldest fall, even thou, and Judah with thee?
But Amaziah would not hear; for it came of God, that he might deliver them into the hand of their enemies, because they sought after the gods of Edom.

And Joash the king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth–shemesh, and brought him to Jerusalem, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.
And he took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obed–edom, and the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria.
Now after the time that Amaziah did turn away from following the Lord they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem; and he fled to Lachish: but they sent to Lachish after him, and slew him there.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, yet not like David his father: he did according to all things as Joash his father did.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.
Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.

text.text: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.

entries.commentary: Amaziah began to reign at twenty and five years old and reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High, but not with a perfect heart. As soon as the kingdom was established he slew the servants that had killed his father the king. He slew the murderers but he did not slay their children, because it is written in the law of Moses that the fathers shall not die for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin. This is a foundational law: a man answers for his own sin, not for another man's.

Amaziah gathered Judah and Benjamin, numbered them from twenty years old and upward, and found three hundred thousand choice men able to go to war. He also hired a hundred thousand mighty men out of Israel for a hundred talents of silver. A man of the Most High came and told him not to let the army of Israel go with him, for the Most High was not with Israel, with all the children of Ephraim. Because of the sin of Ephraim the Most High had cast them off and was not dealing with them, so their help would only bring defeat. When Amaziah asked what to do about the hundred talents he had already paid, the prophet told him the Most High is able to give him much more than that. Amaziah obeyed, separated the army of Ephraim to go home, and they went home in great anger.

Amaziah strengthened himself, led his people to the valley of salt, and smote ten thousand of the children of Seir, and cast down another ten thousand from the top of the rock. But he brought back the gods of the children of Seir, set them up to be his own gods, bowed to them, and burned incense to them. This is the divided heart in action. The Most High gave him the victory, and he responded by grabbing the idols of the people he had just defeated. So the anger of the Most High was kindled against him. The Most High sent a prophet who asked why he sought after gods that could not even deliver their own people out of his hand. This is why counsel is important. The prophet was trying to counsel Amaziah to destroy the idols, and instead Amaziah threatened him and told him to forbear, be quiet. The prophet forbore, but said the Most High had determined to destroy him because he had done this and had not hearkened to counsel.

Amaziah took advice and sent to Joash king of Israel saying, Come, let us see one another in the face. Joash answered with a parable of the thistle and the cedar, telling him his heart lifted him up to boast, and to abide at home rather than meddle to his hurt. Amaziah would not hear, for it came of the Most High, that he might deliver them into the hand of their enemies because they had sought the gods of Edom. Judah was put to the worse before Israel, and they fled every man to his tent. Joash took Amaziah, came to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem four hundred cubits. He took all the gold and silver and the vessels found in the house of the Most High, and the treasures of the king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria. The two kingdoms had real animosity, calling each other another nation, brother stealing the vessels out of his own brother's temple.

Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash king of Israel. From the time he turned away from following the Most High they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish, but they sent after him and slew him there. They brought him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah. When a man departs from the Most High, the protection departs with him.

Amaziah the son of Joash began to reign over Judah at twenty-five and reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High, yet not like David his father, meaning he did not serve with a perfect heart. When the kingdom was confirmed, he slew the servants who had killed his father, but did not slay their children, according to the law of Moses that every man is put to death for his own sin. -
Amaziah slew ten thousand of Edom in the valley of salt and took Selah by war, calling its name Joktheel unto this day.

Amaziah sent to Jehoash king of Israel to face one another in battle, and Jehoash answered with the parable of the thistle and the cedar, warning him to stay home lest he fall. Amaziah would not hear, so the two faced one another at Bethshemesh, and Judah was put to the worse before Israel and fled. Jehoash broke down the wall of Jerusalem, took the gold, silver, and vessels from the house of the Most High and the king's house, took hostages, and returned to Samaria.

Jehoash slept with his fathers and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place. Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash, and a conspiracy was made against him in Jerusalem so that he fled to Lachish and was slain there. The people took Azariah, sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.

Jeroboam the son of Joash, Jeroboam II, began to reign over Israel and reigned forty-one years, doing evil and not departing from the sins of the first Jeroboam. He restored the coast of Israel according to the word spoken by Jonah the son of Amittai, for the Most High saw the bitter affliction of Israel and would not blot out their name. The Most High saved them by the hand of Jeroboam, who recovered Damascus and Hamath, and when he slept with his fathers Zechariah his son reigned in his place. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The seven nations cast out before Israel, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, greater and mightier than Israel, are Hamitic nations. Thou shalt smite them and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them. Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read.

Neither shalt thou make marriages with them: the Most High forbids marrying outside the nation. The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel; a spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with. They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.
Thus shall ye deal with them: destroy their altars, break down their images, cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire. Nothing of their worship was to be spared or adopted.

For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: this is one of the most uplifting scriptures in the book, and it should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently. Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

The Lord did not choose Israel for their number, for ye were the fewest of all people: only threescore and ten souls came out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, as Genesis records, some places reading seventy and some counting seventy-five. But because the Lord loved you: the Most High needs no other reason, he simply loved us, and we should never apologize for that. He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. This is the same teaching as the new testament: loving the Most High is keeping his commandments, and refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes. From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. The Lord will take away from thee all sickness and put none of the evil diseases of Egypt upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. That still reigns true today: keep the commandments and the Most High will keep you from the diseases of modern-day Egypt, and if you do catch something, he will revive you and bring you back to your health.

Thou shalt consume all the people which the Lord thy God shall deliver thee; thine eye shall have no pity upon them, neither shalt thou serve their gods, for that will be a snare unto thee. Those days are coming back when Christ returns.

If thou shalt say in thine heart, these nations are more than I: fear them not, but remember what the Lord did unto Pharaoh and unto all Egypt, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the stretched out arm; so shall he do unto all the people of whom thou art afraid. The Lord will send the hornet among them until even those that hide themselves are destroyed, and he will put out those nations before thee by little and little, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee. He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, and thou shalt destroy their name from under heaven. There is no way to read [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) and still say God loves everybody; that idea is being drunk on Christianity, not reading the book.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: desire not the silver or gold that is on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs, and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol. The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
Graven images, idols and other pagan things to be burned with fire and the material it is made out of is not to be salvaged.
Abstain from every evil thing when at war against your enemies.
Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.
You should not refuse to be corrected and reproved by the righteous among you.
